threats.title: Credential stuffing and brute-force attacks
Offline cracking of stolen password hashes
Weak or previously breached passwords
Account enumeration
Session fixation after login
One-time code guessing and SIM-swap interception
Account takeover with a single compromised factor

controls.title: Hash passwords with Argon2id (or bcrypt/scrypt as fallback)
controls.ai_rule: Hash passwords only with Argon2id from a maintained library (bcrypt or scrypt if unavailable); never use MD5/SHA-* for passwords and never store or log a plaintext password.

verify.description: No md5/sha1/sha256 calls applied to password variables.
Stored password values begin with the $argon2id$ prefix.

controls.title: Rate-limit and throttle authentication attempts
controls.ai_rule: Every login, OTP-verification and password-reset endpoint must be rate-limited per account and per IP; never write an authentication endpoint without throttling.

verify.description: N+1 rapid failed logins for one account are rejected or delayed.
Auth route handlers are registered behind a rate-limit middleware.

controls.title: Enforce minimum length and block breached passwords
controls.ai_rule: Password policy: minimum 12 characters, maximum at least 64, no composition rules, and reject passwords found in breach lists; validate on the server, not only the client.

verify.description: An 11-character password and a known-breached password are both rejected.

controls.title: Issue a new session identifier on login
controls.ai_rule: On successful login or privilege change, regenerate the session ID / issue new tokens and invalidate the previous session.

verify.description: Session cookie value changes after a successful login.

controls.title: Short-lived, single-use, rate-limited one-time codes
controls.ai_rule: One-time codes: generate with a CSPRNG, expire in 10 minutes or less, single use, invalidate after 5 failed attempts, compare in constant time.

verify.description: A used or expired code is rejected; the 6th wrong attempt invalidates the code.

controls.title: Offer multi-factor authentication (require it at higher assurance)
controls.ai_rule: Design authentication so a second factor (passkey/WebAuthn or TOTP) can be enforced; admin accounts must always require MFA.

verify.description: MFA enrollment exists and is enforced for admin roles.

controls.title: Return identical responses for unknown and existing accounts
controls.ai_rule: Login, signup and password-reset responses must not reveal whether an account exists: same message, same status code, comparable timing.

verify.description: Reset request for unknown vs. known email returns identical status and body.

controls.title: No security questions or password hints
controls.ai_rule: Never implement security questions or password hints for account recovery.

verify.description: Recovery flow uses a time-limited token sent to a verified channel only.

threats.title: Cross-site scripting (XSS)
Clickjacking
Traffic downgraded to HTTP or intercepted (SSL stripping, mixed content)
A compromised third-party script runs with full page access
Open redirects used for phishing or token theft
Sensitive pages cached by browsers or shared proxies

controls.title: Encode output by context and avoid dangerous DOM sinks
controls.ai_rule: Never use innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, document.write, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, v-html, eval or new Function with dynamic data; rely on framework escaping, and sanitize with DOMPurify when HTML is unavoidable.

verify.description: No dynamic data flows into HTML sinks or eval.

controls.title: Strict Content Security Policy
controls.ai_rule: Do not add inline scripts or event-handler attributes; scripts load from our origin or carry the CSP nonce; never add unsafe-inline or unsafe-eval to script-src.

verify.description: HTML responses carry a CSP without unsafe-inline/unsafe-eval in script-src.

controls.title: Security headers (HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy)
controls.ai_rule: Keep the security-headers middleware on every response (HSTS, nosniff, frame-ancestors, Referrer-Policy) and never remove or weaken it.

verify.description: Responses include HSTS, nosniff, X-Frame-Options and Referrer-Policy.

controls.title: HTTPS everywhere, no mixed content
controls.ai_rule: Load every resource and call every API over https://; never hardcode http:// URLs except localhost in development.

verify.description: No http:// resource or API URLs other than localhost.

controls.title: Minimize third-party scripts and pin them with Subresource Integrity
controls.ai_rule: Prefer npm packages over CDN script tags; any external <script> must have integrity and crossorigin attributes unless the provider forbids SRI.

verify.description: External script tags carry integrity attributes.

controls.title: Allow only safe, relative redirect targets
controls.ai_rule: Never redirect to a URL taken directly from user input; accept only relative paths starting with a single "/" or an allow-listed destination.

verify.description: No res.redirect() with request parameters.

controls.title: Prevent caching of sensitive responses
controls.ai_rule: Responses containing personal or sensitive data must send Cache-Control no-store.

verify.description: Account pages respond with Cache-Control no-store.

threats.title: Broken object-level authorization (accessing other users' records by ID)
Broken function-level authorization (calling admin or other privileged endpoints)
Mass assignment and excessive data exposure
Unrestricted resource consumption
Injection through unvalidated input
Cross-origin data theft through permissive CORS
Internal details leaked through errors, debug modes or version headers
Forgotten, undocumented or old API versions left exposed
Credentials or tokens exposed in URLs
Abuse of over-privileged or leaked third-party API credentials

controls.title: Check object-level authorization on every request that takes a resource ID
controls.ai_rule: Every handler that loads or changes a record by ID must check that the current user is allowed to access that specific record (scope the query by owner/tenant); being authenticated is not enough.

verify.description: User A requesting user B's resource by ID gets 403/404.

controls.title: Deny-by-default function-level authorization
controls.ai_rule: Apply authorization middleware to all routes by default and explicitly mark public ones; check roles/permissions on the server for every privileged action, never only in the UI.

verify.description: A regular user calling an admin endpoint gets 403.

controls.title: Validate requests against a schema and return explicit response shapes
controls.ai_rule: Validate every request with a schema that rejects unknown fields; never pass req.body directly to an ORM create/update; return explicit response objects, never whole database models.

verify.description: No ORM create/update called with the raw request body.
Sending role=admin in a profile update has no effect.

controls.title: Rate limits, pagination caps, payload limits and timeouts
controls.ai_rule: List endpoints must enforce a maximum page size; apply rate limits, request body size limits and timeouts to all API routes.

verify.description: limit=100000 is clamped; exceeding the rate limit returns 429.

controls.title: Strict CORS allow-list
controls.ai_rule: Configure CORS with an explicit list of allowed origins; never reflect the request Origin, never allow "null", and never use "*" with credentials.

verify.description: A request from https://evil.example gets no Access-Control-Allow-Origin header.

controls.title: Scoped, revocable, per-client credentials for third parties
controls.ai_rule: Third-party API credentials must be per-client, scoped to minimum permissions, stored hashed, revocable and rate-limited per client.

verify.description: Each third-party key has scopes and can be revoked without affecting others.

controls.title: Generic errors, no debug mode or version headers in production
controls.ai_rule: API error responses must not include stack traces, SQL errors or internal paths; return a generic message with a request ID and log details server-side; disable X-Powered-By and debug modes.

verify.description: A forced 500 error returns no stack trace.

controls.title: Keep an API inventory and retire old versions
controls.ai_rule: Document new endpoints in the API spec; do not add debug, test or temporary endpoints without removing them before merge.

verify.description: Routes in production match the documented API inventory.

controls.title: Send credentials in headers, never in URLs
controls.ai_rule: Accept API keys and tokens only from headers or cookies, never from query string parameters.

verify.description: No req.query.token / api_key / access_token reads.

threats.title: SQL injection
Excessive damage from a compromised application account
Credentials leaked from source code or images
Interception of database traffic
Exposure of sensitive data from stolen disks, snapshots or backups

controls.title: Use parameterized queries or a safe query builder / ORM
controls.ai_rule: Never build SQL with string concatenation or template literals; always use bound parameters, and pick dynamic identifiers (columns, sort order) from an allow-list.

verify.description: No query()/execute()/raw() call receives a concatenated or interpolated string.

controls.title: Load database credentials from a secret store, never from source
controls.ai_rule: Never hardcode database credentials or connection strings; read them from environment variables or a secrets manager.

verify.description: No connection string with an inline password in source files.

controls.title: Least-privilege database accounts
controls.ai_rule: The application connects with a least-privilege database user; migrations use a separate account; never connect as root/superuser/admin.

verify.description: Application DB role has no DDL/superuser rights.

controls.title: Encrypt database connections with verified TLS
controls.ai_rule: Database connections must use TLS with certificate verification; never disable certificate checks (e.g. rejectUnauthorized: false, sslmode=require without verify).

verify.description: No rejectUnauthorized false in DB client config.

controls.title: Encrypt sensitive data at rest and in backups
controls.ai_rule: Sensitive fields (IDs, health, financial data) are encrypted at rest; keys come from a KMS, never from source code.

verify.description: Storage encryption is enabled on the DB instance and its backups.

threats.title: Upload of executable or malicious content
Path traversal through the file name
Resource exhaustion through huge files or decompression bombs
Stored XSS by serving uploads as HTML/SVG from the app origin
Malware distribution to other users

controls.title: Validate type by file content against an allow-list
controls.ai_rule: Validate uploads by file content (magic bytes) against an allow-list of types; never trust the extension or client Content-Type; re-encode images server-side.

verify.description: A PHP/HTML file renamed to .jpg is rejected.

controls.title: Generate server-side file names; never use the client file name in paths
controls.ai_rule: Store uploads under a server-generated random name; never build a filesystem path or object key from the user-supplied file name.

verify.description: No path.join / open() using the uploaded file's original name.

controls.title: Store uploads outside the web root with no execute permission
controls.ai_rule: Store uploads in private object storage or a non-executable directory outside the web root; serve them via short-lived signed URLs or a controlled download handler.

verify.description: Upload location is not reachable as a static path and buckets are private.

controls.title: Serve user files safely (separate origin, attachment, nosniff)
controls.ai_rule: Serve user uploads from a separate domain with Content-Disposition: attachment (except safe images), explicit Content-Type and X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff; never inline user SVG/HTML on the app origin.

verify.description: Download responses include nosniff and attachment headers.

controls.title: Enforce size limits and guard against decompression bombs
controls.ai_rule: Enforce a maximum upload size at the server, and cap decompressed size, entry count and image dimensions before processing any archive or image.

verify.description: Body-size limit is configured on the upload route.
An upload above the limit returns 413.

controls.title: Scan uploaded files for malware
controls.ai_rule: Quarantine uploads and make them available to other users only after a malware scan passes.

verify.description: The upload pipeline has a scan step before files are published.

threats.title: Forged payment webhooks mark unpaid orders as paid
Price or amount tampering by the client
Double fulfilment from retries, replays or race conditions
Card testing (carding) through the checkout
Card data leaked through logs, analytics or databases

controls.title: Verify webhook signatures and process each event once
controls.ai_rule: Payment webhooks must verify the provider signature on the raw request body with the webhook secret, reject stale timestamps, and ignore event IDs that were already processed.

verify.description: A webhook with an invalid signature returns 400 and changes nothing.

controls.title: Compute amounts on the server and verify them before fulfilment
controls.ai_rule: Never accept prices, totals or currency from the client; compute amounts on the server from the catalog and verify the paid amount and currency before fulfilling an order.

verify.description: Changing the price in the checkout request does not change the charged amount.

controls.title: Never log or store card data; keep only provider tokens and the last 4 digits
controls.ai_rule: Never log, persist or send to analytics any card number, CVV or full payment payload; store only provider IDs plus brand and last 4 digits.

verify.description: Logs and analytics events from a test checkout contain no card data.

controls.title: Idempotent payment and fulfilment operations
controls.ai_rule: Create charges with idempotency keys and make order fulfilment idempotent (unique constraint or transaction on the payment ID) so it can never run twice.

verify.description: Delivering the same payment-succeeded event twice concurrently fulfils once.

controls.title: Throttle and screen payment attempts against card testing
controls.ai_rule: Rate-limit payment and card-setup attempts per user, IP and card fingerprint, and keep the provider's fraud screening enabled.

verify.description: Repeated declined attempts trigger throttling.
